text:
Ifmyante wrote: Our traders did predict the turn there, and made a few years worth of profit on it, but that's not the point.

The evil here is the ferocity with which the move was made, forcing
price to slip and gap past all the stops, intentionally bankrupting so
many retailers and brokers.

The people who will bail out anybody in trouble are the same people who
made it happen, the ones who print money out of thin air to take control
 of the people and companies they've destroyed, the people who start
wars and create the money to loan to the warring countries, who own the
weapons companies, the rebuilding companies, and the companies who will
take control of the natural resources of the countries who lost and won,
 the people who own the pharmaceutical companies which put sterilising
agents into inoculations, the people who own the media which tells you
that all of this is OK, and that we must fear everybody except them, the
 people who control everything your governments do!

We are firmly in the grip of the moochers and looters. We have been for
 some time. Until we can get people to value production and make it
completely illegal to bludgeon someone else for money, things will stay
as they are. It won't matter if you turn everything over to the people
as most of the people I see and know have the entitlement mentality of :
 well I pay my taxes I want X. I deserve X, the people who have more
than me owe me X. If you force people to work for X (like you or I
must) then you're impinging on their rights (this goes for both rich and
 poor they're the same type of looter). If you suggest a better way for
 them to get X they tell you that you're part of the problem and you
don't know how rough they've had it or "its easy for you". Its getting
to the point that I don't bother discussing how to make things better as
 people seem devoid of basic reason or logic. Or worse they know but
try to bullshit you that they don't.

There's a lot of the "money for nothing and the chicks for free"
attitude going on in all levels of society right now. Its funny, I
don't remember being taught any of this in school but people have
learned it from somewhere. My little girl is being taught the benefits
of being kind, empathetic, caring, disciplined, productive etc. As far
as I know we all got this training yet most of us are tempted by the
easy route somewhere down the line and then choose to remain there.
There is no good world for anyone without effort. Its an unbreakable
logical rule garbage in = garbage out. Worse is that society,
governments etc coddle and encourage such ideas. When people tell
others to get off their ass and work to create the world they want to
live in they are called harsh, soulless, Dr. Spocks, nazi, conservative
everything except pragmatist :).

A country should be run as a long term project not a 2-4 year scam. A
pure democracy is: The sheep asking the wolves whats for dinner. If a
system such as this were to be realized I would hope it would be based
on rule of law. Without absolute rights we're at the whim of our
brother and we'd be exchanging the current scum for new scum. I would
be interested to see what legal system PBD would enact as well as who
would fill the void after the current overlords are removed. Its one
thing to get rid of them but thinking we're going to keep their
infrastructure when the go without a fight is a bit worrisome. Whats
the contingency. Who will build the new system. Who will pay the
builders. How do we make sure that the new people who lead the new
system don't take advantage and lead us back to square one. If I were
asked to vote on whether we should use banana bucks vs energy credits vs
 bitcoins for a new exchange system what qualifies me to vote on that
choice? Same goes for infrastructure, court system political system,
voting transparency etc. We need to pass some of the heavy lifting to
the experts or we will spend every waking moment at the polling
stations. We have to be able to trust our experts and advisers and to
do so we must pick and pay them well. However, how do we know they have
 the best interest of the country in mind and who decides the best
interest? If you stop in at Tim Hortons here (coffee shop) you'll hear
50 different opinions concerning any topic how do we narrow these down
for voting purposes? Just a few thoughts. I'm not against the idea, it
 just seems like a whole wack of hurtles before we even get into the
more complicated issues. Cheers.

author: knight
text:
Thanks IF. Often i get confused is whether i should mark QM as a line
 or box like i draw earlier. Coz if you put box Sl is too large. If i
put line my sl can be very near.

do you hv any suggestion for this?

author: Ifmyante
text:
A line is not the answer.

Certainly, you may draw a line, but you must then go into the LTF to
find a DBR/RBD on the right side of the LL/HH swing which covers that
line. That RBD/DBR will be your box.

You can scalp from each of these, knowing that it may only be a scalp.

If you're simply setting a PO, then you must set your stop beyond the FL the HH/LL is a reaction to.

For obvious reasons, I can't go into any greater detail than that
